name: build_node_list_from_table
description: Library code that walks a null-terminated pointer table taken from a global, creating a node for each entry through library calls and linking the nodes into a list. It stores the first node as the list head and returns early if a node cannot be created.

name: link_nodes_from_pointer_table
description: Library code that loops over a null-terminated table of pointers, allocating a node per entry via library calls, storing each entry in its node and linking the node into the list. It records the list head and returns the last subroutine result, or zero if a node allocation fails.

name: link_nodes_until_table_end
description: Library code that allocates a node for each table entry, stores the entry in the node and links it onto the list, looping until the table terminator is reached. It sets the list head when the loop finishes and returns zero if no node can be obtained.

name: retire_current_list_head
description: Library code that checks whether the list head is the only remaining entry; if so it finishes that entry through three library calls, otherwise it sends two messages for the current entry and advances the head to the next linked node. It sends a final message to the caller's parameter in both cases.

name: advance_cursor_pointer_and_notify
description: Library code that passes the entry referenced by the current cursor to a subroutine together with a global value, then moves the cursor to the entry's next link. It finishes with a further subroutine call.

name: step_list_cursor_or_finish
description: Library code that tests whether the cursor has reached the end of the list; at the end it finishes the entry through library calls, otherwise it notifies two subroutines and moves the cursor to the entry stored in the next link. It closes with a message to the parameter.

name: step_cursor_via_dereference
description: Library code that passes the current cursor entry to a subroutine with a global value, replaces the cursor with the entry pointed to by its link, and makes a final subroutine call. It is the dereferencing variant of the cursor step.

name: append_entry_to_global_list
description: Library code that sets a global status value, notifies subroutines when the list is not empty, allocates a new entry through a library call, copies its data and inserts it at the tail of the global list. It then sets the status to a second value and updates the global list pointer.

name: release_entry_and_relink_list
description: Library code that sets a global status value and, for a list with more than one entry, notifies subroutines and selects the neighbouring link as the new list head. With a single entry it finishes that entry through library calls instead.

name: advance_cursor_with_fallback
description: Library code that passes the current cursor entry to a subroutine and moves the cursor to the entry in its next link, falling back to the first list entry when the list end is reached. It makes one more subroutine call before returning.

name: notify_entry_callbacks_in_sequence
description: Library code that makes one subroutine call and then two more subroutine calls, passing values read from fixed fields of the current entry at offsets 46 and 62 bytes. It runs the steps in a fixed order with no branching.

name: build_entry_array_if_flagged
description: When a global flag is set, library code counts the list entries, allocates an array with one pointer slot per entry, and allocates a block for each entry sized from the entry's own value with a default of four bytes. It returns zero if any allocation fails and one otherwise.

name: build_entry_pointer_array
description: Library code that counts the list entries, allocates a pointer array sized to that count, and fills each slot with a newly allocated block for the matching entry. It returns zero on allocation failure and one on success, and clears the array pointer when the list is empty.

name: allocate_entry_array_after_notify
description: Library code that first passes a value from the current entry to a subroutine, then counts the list entries and allocates an array of pointers, one per entry. It fills the array with per-entry blocks and returns one, or zero when an allocation fails.

name: count_and_allocate_entry_array
description: Library code that counts the links in a pointer chain, allocates an array with one long-word slot per link through a library call, and fills each slot with a block for the matching entry. It returns one on success and zero if any allocation fails.

name: fill_entry_array_from_list
description: Library code that passes the array base to a subroutine, then walks the list allocating a block for each entry and storing its pointer in the array. It returns one when the list is exhausted and zero if an allocation fails.

name: fill_entry_blocks_until_end
description: Library code that walks the list from a given entry, allocating a block for each entry and storing its pointer at the current array index. It stops at the list end or when an allocation fails and returns one or zero accordingly.

name: copy_entries_into_array_slots
description: Library code that walks entries from the current one, passing each to library calls that allocate a block and copy the entry's data into the matching array slot. It returns one when the list ends and zero if an allocation fails.

name: call_library_offset_minus_90
description: Library stub that loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library function at offset minus 90 with no arguments. It is a thin forwarding wrapper with no other logic.

name: dispatch_layout_by_mode
description: Library code that reads a mode byte from a global block and selects one of six fixed sequences of subroutine calls. Each sequence passes coordinate-style values and a shared buffer to the subroutines, and the cases differ only in which calls they make.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Empty library routine whose only instruction is a return, so calling it has no effect. The decompiler output shows no operations at all.

name: allocate_mode_buffers_and_run
description: Library code that allocates four fixed-size buffers through library calls and, if all succeed, allocates four more. It then runs a mode-dependent sequence of subroutine calls using those buffers and returns the last subroutine result, or zero when an allocation fails.

name: run_mode_sequence_after_setup
description: Library code that reads four values through indirect calls, stores the last one through a pointer, and returns zero if any value is zero. Otherwise it runs a mode-dependent number of subroutine calls, one to four, and returns the result of the final call.

name: run_mode_helper_sequence
description: Library code that switches on a mode byte and issues a fixed count of subroutine calls for that mode, from two calls up to five. It returns nothing and only sequences the subroutines.

name: stub_return_only
description: Empty library routine that contains only a return instruction, so it performs no work when called.

name: clear_or_copy_then_check
description: Library code that either zeroes a longword through a pointer or passes a global buffer and a length to a subroutine, depending on a global value. It then calls a status subroutine and maps a failure value of minus one to zero.

name: copy_buffer_and_check_status
description: Library code that passes a global buffer and a length to a subroutine, then calls a second subroutine and maps its failure value of minus one to zero. It returns the normalised status.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: Empty library routine that returns at once without any operations. The decompiler shows only a return statement.

name: update_four_entries_and_check
description: Unless the mode byte equals four, library code stores fixed 16-bit values into a field of four structures and then calls a subroutine on each structure. It returns one only when all four calls succeed, otherwise zero.

name: check_three_calls_succeeded
description: Library code that calls a function pointer three times in sequence and returns one only when none of the calls returns minus one. It stops at the first failing call and returns zero.

name: check_two_calls_succeeded
description: Library code that calls a function pointer twice and returns one only when neither call returns minus one. It stops after the first failing call and returns zero.

name: check_single_call_not_failed
description: Library code that calls a function pointer once and returns true unless the result is minus one.

name: stub_return_success
description: Library routine that returns the constant one and performs no other work.

name: process_entries_until_failure
description: Library code that loops indefinitely, taking an entry from a structure and passing it with a parameter to a subroutine. It returns zero if the subroutine fails; when no entry is present it calls a library function with a single-bit mask built from a byte field of the structure.

name: stub_return_failure
description: Library routine that returns zero immediately and does nothing else. Its only caller is a reschedule routine.

name: dispatch_state_handler_result
description: Library code that branches on a numeric state field: state four calls one subroutine, state 64 returns the result of a second subroutine, and state 512 calls a subroutine and returns zero. Any other state calls a subroutine and returns one.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: Routine that invokes one subroutine with no arguments and returns without a value. It is a plain forwarding wrapper.

name: call_helper_return_zero
description: Calls one subroutine with no arguments and returns zero regardless of what the subroutine returns.

name: call_two_helpers_return_one
description: Calls two subroutines in sequence with no arguments and then returns one.

name: send_mode_dependent_callbacks
description: Library code that calls subroutines three times with the given parameter, adds a fourth call unless the mode byte equals one, then makes two final subroutine calls. One final call passes a field of the parameter structure and the other passes the constant one.

name: format_four_access_flags
description: Library code that derives a four-bit flag value from a byte field and calls a subroutine once per flag with the flag position and a shared text table. The referenced labels are archived, deleteable, readable and writeable.

name: format_indexed_flag_label
description: Copies a fixed short string into a stack buffer, selects one of two label strings according to a flag argument, and formats the result with a string routine. It then emits two text items at fixed positions using a character picked by index and the chosen label.

name: prepare_format_argument_buffer
description: Builds a stack argument block from a parameter field and passes it, with a template string, to a string-formatting routine. It then makes two further subroutine calls.

name: measure_null_terminated_length
description: Counts the bytes of a null-terminated string from the given address and returns the count without the terminator.

name: count_bytes_until_null
description: Register-based variant that advances an index from a base address until it reaches a zero byte, then returns that index as the string length.

name: copy_c_string_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a source string to a destination buffer one at a time, including the terminating zero byte, and stops after writing it.

name: copy_fixed_byte_count
description: Copies a fixed number of bytes from a source address to a destination address, one byte at a time, using the count passed in.

name: copy_bytes_until_count
description: Register-based byte copy that moves bytes from one buffer to another until a counter reaches the limit held in a register.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings character by character, stopping at the first difference or at a terminator, and returns whether the final characters match.

name: match_strings_at_terminator
description: Register-based string comparison that advances through two strings together and stops at the first zero byte in either one. It returns whether the characters at that point are equal.

name: count_bytes_including_terminator
description: Counts bytes from the given address up to and including the terminating zero byte and returns that count. It is a length routine that reports the terminator as well.

name: issue_three_library_calls
description: Calls a subroutine to obtain a value, then issues three library calls through a library base held in a structure. The calls pass the parameters, one of them reduced by ten, and the obtained value.

name: fill_local_buffer_and_forward
description: Fills a 12-byte local buffer from a global source through a subroutine, then forwards the five arguments together with that buffer to a second subroutine.

name: copy_length_prefixed_string
description: Copies a length-prefixed string into a destination buffer byte by byte and appends a zero terminator. The routine sits in an unreached gap, so the decoded body may be data rather than a called routine.

name: copy_bytes_and_append_zero
description: Register-based loop that copies bytes from a source to a destination up to a limit, then writes a zero terminator after the copied bytes. It is reached only through the decoded gap, so its register setup comes from the caller.

name: initialise_two_records_and_run
description: Fills two structures with field values taken from its parameters, including a pointer linking the second record to the first, then calls two subroutines. It calls a third subroutine with the first record and makes a final subroutine call only when that result is not minus one, returning true in that case.

name: invoke_member_callback_return_one
description: Calls a subroutine with a function pointer read from a structure member at offset 62 and then returns one.

name: issue_offset_adjusted_library_calls
description: Issues three calls through a library base stored in a structure: one with the second argument, one with zero, and one with the third argument plus two values derived from the fifth and sixth parameters, each reduced by ten.

name: call_raw_format_routine
description: Library stub that calls the system RawDoFmt routine through a global base pointer. It passes no arguments of its own, so its work depends on the registers set by the caller.

name: store_byte_at_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of a data register to the address held in a pointer register. It is a single-store subroutine with no other logic.

name: call_library_offset_minus_36
description: Library stub that calls the library function at offset minus 36 from a base pointer read from a global table. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: call_library_offset_minus_72
description: Library stub that calls the library function at offset minus 72 from a base pointer read from a global table. It takes no arguments and returns nothing.

name: stub_entry_return_zero
description: Program entry routine that returns zero immediately, with no other operations.

name: store_two_fields_in_record
description: Stores two register values into fixed fields, at byte offsets 34 and 38, of the record addressed by a data register, then returns.

name: increment_counter_clear_flag_bit
description: Increments a 16-bit counter at one fixed offset of a record and clears bit three of a flag byte at another offset. Nothing else is done.

name: decrement_counter_call_helper
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter at offset 32 of a record. When the counter reaches zero and flag bit three is set, it calls the bit reader used by the depacker and returns its result; otherwise it returns zero.

name: finish_counter_and_call_library
description: When the counter at offset 32 is zero, reads a value from offset 38 and calls two library functions through the base pointer at offset 34, then returns that value. Otherwise it sets flag bit three and returns zero.

name: load_value_and_call_libraries
description: Reads a value from offset 38 of a passed record, calls two library functions through a library base held in a register, and returns the value. It is entered from the bit reader routine.

name: stub_return_zero_handler
description: Routine that returns zero immediately and performs no other work. It is reached through a pointer in data rather than from direct calls.

name: initialise_hardware_and_graphics
description: Start-up routine that clears a block of memory, writes initial values to the interrupt-enable, DMA-control and copper-pointer registers, and waits on hardware status bits. It then opens graphics.library through the exec library and stores the returned base, calling a further library vector afterwards.

name: locate_character_and_fill_table
description: Walks a text table of letters, digits and punctuation one character at a time, using a step of two per character, to find the index of a given character. It stores that index as an address offset, then copies a 20-entry block and fills a table from a wrapping index.

name: run_blitter_draw_loop
description: Updates two wrapping accumulators, then programs the blitter control, mask, pointer and modulo registers in a nested loop. Each pass waits for the blitter busy flag before setting its source, destination and size, and takes its values from a table with an advancing index.

name: toggle_bit_then_wait_loop
description: Toggles one bit, chosen by the low three bits of a data register, in a byte at the address held in a pointer register. It then keeps only bits ten and eleven of a fixed word and runs the thirty-step wait loop.

name: mask_word_then_wait_loop
description: Keeps only bits ten and eleven of a 16-bit word at a fixed offset from the address register and then runs the thirty-step wait loop. It does not change any byte.

name: run_thirty_step_wait_loop
description: Runs thirty iterations, each calling one subroutine and then calling a second subroutine repeatedly until it returns zero. It returns nothing and sets no values.

name: start_blitter_copy_setup
description: Waits for the blitter busy flag to clear, then sets the blitter control to a plain copy using all four channels with zero shift and clears one modulo register. It loads the source and destination pointers from its arguments and starts a blit of a fixed one-word-wide rectangle.

name: fill_block_from_table_count
description: Looks up a count in a byte table for the index in a data register, or uses sixteen when the index is zero. It calls subroutines and then fills that many longwords at the destination with a fixed constant, returning without filling when the table count is zero.

name: fill_longs_with_constant
description: Fills a run of longwords at the destination address with a fixed constant, with the number of entries taken from the data register.

name: poll_until_helper_returns_zero
description: Repeatedly calls a subroutine and loops until the subroutine returns zero. It has no other effect besides this repetition.

name: swap_long_and_split_halves
description: Exchanges a 32-bit value between two globals, then stores the low and high words of the value taken from the first global into two further globals.

name: swap_long_and_split_halves
description: Exchanges a 32-bit value between two globals, then stores the low and high words of the value taken from the first global into two further globals. It is identical to the routine at the neighbouring address.

name: setup_four_audio_channels
description: Programs the four audio channel register blocks in turn: each gets the same sample pointer, a length of thirteen words and a volume of 64, and a period that rises by four per channel from 2000. It then writes the DMA control value that enables the four audio channels.

name: increment_strided_byte_triplets
description: Adds one, two and three to three bytes at offsets 0, 8 and 16 of each 24-byte record, walking 110 records from a fixed starting address.

name: initialise_two_lookup_tables
description: Fills 140 six-longword entries with fixed longword constants, then fills 110 eight-byte entries with a counting pattern. In each eight-byte entry one byte steps up by two, a second byte holds a running sum, and the last byte is zero.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: When the destination pointer is set, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a structure into it. It then calls a function through a pointer held in a register, and is one of the routines the maximum-search code uses.

name: echo_command_entry_setup
description: Entry routine of the echo command. It walks a linked list to find the largest stored value, fills a buffer with a sequence of longwords whose header comes from that value, and uses library calls and a stack buffer to set up the output.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: When the destination pointer is set, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset in a structure into it. It then calls a function through a pointer held in a register, and is one of the routines the maximum-search code uses.

name: parse_loadwb_command_line
description: Entry point for the loadwb command. It allocates a task record, tokenises its command-line text into an argument array that handles quoted strings and star escapes for newline and escape characters, then frees its resources and returns a status.

name: release_task_resources_and_return
description: Saves its argument as the status in the current task record, then conditionally closes a DOS handle, replies to a message, frees memory and closes a library through library calls. It returns the saved status.

name: start_workbench_tool_with_report
description: Checks library and task state through many library calls, then starts a Workbench-related tool. It reports a missing resident tag or a start error code, and checks an argument against a debug option when the first argument equals two.

name: compare_strings_three_way
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte and returns minus one if the first sorts before the second, one if it sorts after, and zero when they are equal.

name: build_resident_list_from_table
description: Walks a null-terminated chain of table entries, allocating an eight-byte node for each through a library call and copying into it a value found by a resident-module search. The nodes are linked in order and the head of the new list is returned.

name: match_release_string_and_pad
description: Compares a global text against the buffer and, when the buffer character at position 20 is a '2' and the text matches, writes a period and four spaces at position 17. The text is the Workbench release string, and the routine returns its incoming byte register unchanged.

name: write_period_and_spaces
description: Writes a period followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes at offset 17 of the buffer addressed by the address register.

name: skip_matching_global_prefix
description: Advances through the buffer while its characters match a global text, stopping when the global text ends. It returns nothing and leaves the buffer pointer past the matched prefix.

name: stub_empty_routine_loadwb
description: Empty routine of four instructions that performs no operation and returns. Three other routines reference it.

name: forward_with_stack_slot
description: Forwards its two arguments to a subroutine together with a pointer to the caller's stack argument area, then returns.

name: format_text_and_write_output
description: Calls the system formatting routine through a global base pointer to fill a 140-byte buffer. It measures the result as the complement of a countdown and passes the buffer and that length to a subroutine when the length is nonzero.

name: validate_disk_bitmap_entry
description: Entry routine of the Disk-Validator program. It sets up counters and a status string, then walks ranges of bitmap bits, comparing the bit for each block against a second flag and counting the places where they differ, with library calls in between.

name: clear_block_and_open_library
description: Program entry that clears a block of longwords starting at a base-relative address and saves a register value and a global pointer. It calls a subroutine when a flag bit is set, then loads a library base through a library vector and takes one of two follow-up paths depending on the result.

name: allocate_demo_picture_buffers
description: Allocates five buffers of fixed sizes through library calls, each with a memory-type flag, and stores every handle in a global. It then runs a sequence of subroutine calls, repeating part of the setup when its argument is below two, and the routine references the demo.pic text.

name: start_copper_list_from_record
description: Starts the copper on the copper list whose address is read from offset 38 of a global record, by calling the copper start routine with that address.

name: setup_timing_constants_and_interrupts
description: Calls two subroutines, passes four constants with table pointers to further subroutines, and writes a fixed value to a global flag. It touches the interrupt-enable hardware register and so changes interrupt state.

name: allocate_block_and_offset_table
description: Allocates a 1152-byte block through a library call and stores its address in a global. It then fills an eight-entry array with addresses stepping by 144 bytes, calls a subroutine and stores two addresses derived from another global.

name: store_word_and_call_helper
description: Stores the constant 399 into a 16-bit global and then calls a subroutine with no arguments.

name: call_helper_with_block_size
description: Calls a subroutine with the block address stored in a global and the constant 1152, which is the size of that block.

name: call_helpers_with_global_pointers
description: Calls one subroutine with a pointer read from a global and then a second subroutine with another pointer read from a global, each as a single argument.

name: call_library_offset_minus_300
description: Passes the low word of its argument, together with a value held in a global base, to the library function at offset minus 300 through a library stub. Nothing else is done.

name: call_one_helper_no_args
description: Calls one subroutine with no arguments and returns without a value, adding nothing else.

name: lookup_pair_and_call_helper
description: Compares the second argument with each of two table values and, on a match, calls a subroutine with the corresponding entry from a second table. It stores the matched index in a global, which is two when nothing matches.

name: swap_globals_and_call_helper
description: Swaps two 32-bit globals and then calls a subroutine with the new values of both.

name: open_graphics_and_intuition_libs
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries through library calls and stores each base in a global. It calls a fallback subroutine when an open returns zero, and stores bit two of a field from the graphics base in a global.

name: wait_for_status_then_call
description: Polls a subroutine until it returns one, two or three, calling a second subroutine between polls. It then calls a third subroutine with a global value and a pointer to a record field.

name: load_pic_and_classify_state
description: Loads the load.pic file through subroutines, then waits for a global flag to clear, bounded to 350000 steps. It sets a state from one to three depending on which fixed range two global shorts fall into, leaves it at zero otherwise, and returns that state.

name: initialise_records_and_run_loop
description: Installs two function pointers and three constants into globals, clears a zero-terminated short array, and initialises sixteen records from a table. It then loops, toggling a flag and calling subroutines for two records and then for eight, until a subroutine returns zero.

name: run_slot_update_loop
description: Runs while a stop flag is clear and a counter is nonzero, advancing two countdown values and updating sixteen slots by comparing table bytes. Codes at or above 100 select entries in a sorted list of up to nineteen pending values, and the routine returns when the stop flag is set.

name: stub_empty_gap_return
description: Empty one-instruction routine that only returns. It sits in an unreached gap of the executable, so it is likely padding decoded as code.

name: initialise_slot_positions_loop
description: When the first subroutine reports zero, initialises eighteen slot values from subroutine results masked to three bits and then loops positioning slots until a subroutine returns zero. Otherwise it positions slots relative to a reference value while a stop flag is clear and a counter is nonzero, returning zero or one.

name: fill_two_short_arrays
description: Fills two short arrays for a count given by the parameter. The first array receives each subroutine result reduced modulo thirteen and offset by 232, and the second receives the next subroutine result reduced modulo nine.

name: update_short_arrays_with_decay
description: For each of a count of entries, adds one to a stored value and subtracts it from a paired value. When the difference is negative, the first array is set to zero and the second to half the negated value. It returns the first value computed in the loop.

name: run_demo_picture_sequence
description: Runs a fixed startup of library and subroutine calls that reference demo.pic, then loops over a subroutine until it returns zero or a stop flag is set. Afterwards it copies one global pointer into another and updates a flag.

name: initialise_four_buffer_entries
description: Computes four buffer addresses by adding 300 and 32000 bytes per index to two base globals, calls a subroutine for each address pair, and copies four globals from the bases into a second set of globals.

name: load_block_with_read_wrapper
description: Requests a block with the fixed identifier 1005 through a subroutine and returns minus one if that fails. Otherwise it reads 32000 bytes into a buffer through the read wrapper, calls a further subroutine and returns zero.

name: load_font_and_sprite_files
description: Loads several data files whose names include font.dat, land0 and sprites0.dat. Each is opened through a subroutine with the fixed identifier 1005, read into a buffer with a fixed byte count, and then closed.

name: load_resource_into_buffers
description: Opens a resource with the identifier 1005 and, when the open succeeds, reads 40000 bytes into the second argument and 64 bytes into a global buffer before closing it.

name: rotate_and_merge_word_planes
description: When the row argument lies in a valid range, rotates each source word by a nibble-derived amount and merges the rotated words into four interleaved planes of the destination buffer using AND masks and OR. The number of rows processed depends on the position.

name: merge_rotated_mask_into_tiles
description: When the row argument lies in a valid range, rotates a sixteen-word mask block by a nibble-derived amount and ANDs and ORs the rotated words into four interleaved planes of the map tile buffer, repeating for sixteen rows.

name: stub_unreached_helper_wrapper
description: Small wrapper in an unreached gap that calls one subroutine and returns its register result. It is probably decoded from data, so its behaviour is not reliable.

name: merge_tile_mask_optional_shift
description: When the row is in range, merges a sixteen-word source block into four interleaved planes of a destination buffer using AND and OR masks, with the source chosen by the second argument. A zero shift nibble takes a path with no rotation, and the routine repeats for twenty-four rows.

name: reorder_table_entry_fields
description: Iterates over 1680 twenty-byte entries of a global table, moving each word and byte field to a new position within its entry in place.

name: shift_hundred_bytes_left_three
description: Shifts each of the hundred bytes in a fixed buffer left by three bits, in place.

name: process_ten_by_ten_grid
description: Walks a ten-by-ten grid of table entries, calling a subroutine for each cell with coordinates derived from its row and column and an offset read from the cell's entry. It calls a second subroutine when a flag byte in the buffer is set.

name: call_helper_return_register_pair
description: Calls one subroutine and returns the values in two data registers combined into a single 64-bit result.

name: set_global_pointer_to_buffer
description: Stores the address of a global buffer into a global pointer variable and returns, with no other work.

name: render_string_glyphs_into_buffer
description: Clears two buffers, one with eighty minus-one longwords and one with 320 zero longwords, then draws each character of a global string into a buffer. Each character is copied as five-byte columns from a table indexed by the character minus 32 into four bit-plane rows. The global string pointer is advanced past the text and reset when the end marker is reached.

name: open_resource_with_fallback
description: Opens a resource through a global library vector and, when that succeeds, opens a second resource, stores its handle, sets several global configuration values and clears a flag byte. When the first open fails, it calls two cleanup vectors and returns the result of the second.

name: open_resource_with_fallback
description: Same decoded body as the routine at the lower address: opens a resource through a global library vector and, when that succeeds, opens a second one, stores its handle, sets global configuration values and clears a flag byte. Otherwise it calls two cleanup vectors and returns their result.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry has only one instruction, so the large listing shown is the shared open-resource body decoded from overlapping bytes. No reliable behaviour can be recovered for this entry.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry has only one instruction, so the large listing shown is the shared open-resource body decoded from overlapping bytes. No reliable behaviour can be recovered for this entry.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The entry has only one instruction, so the large listing shown is the shared open-resource body decoded from overlapping bytes. No reliable behaviour can be recovered for this entry.

name: load_sample_file_with_messages
description: Opens and reads a sample file named in the referenced text, allocates memory and writes the interrupt registers through library calls. Its failure paths refer to the not-enough-memory and file-not-found messages. The shown pseudo-code is a shared listing, so the file steps rest on the call list alone.

name: stub_unreached_empty_return
description: One-instruction routine in an unreached gap that only returns. It is likely padding decoded as code.

name: clear_byte_and_return_value
description: Stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the pointer register and returns the eight-byte value passed on the stack. It sits in an unreached gap and is called from six places.

name: reset_interrupts_and_free_memory
description: Writes fixed control values to the interrupt-enable and interrupt-request registers, calls the free-memory library function, and restores three saved globals. The last global is set with a high-bit mask, and the routine returns a combined value from two data registers.

name: dispatch_code_then_clear_byte
description: Compares a byte in a data register with ten and then with one, calling a subroutine for each match. It then stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the record pointer and returns the stacked value. It sits in an unreached gap, so the decoded body may be data.

name: clear_flag_after_optional_call
description: When a byte in the data register equals one, calls a subroutine, then clears a byte at a fixed offset of the record and returns the stacked value. It sits in an unreached gap, so the decoding is less reliable.

name: clear_record_flag_and_return
description: Stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the pointer register and returns the stacked value. It sits in an unreached gap and its decoded body is likely data.

name: clear_record_flag_and_return
description: Stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the pointer register and returns the stacked value. It sits in an unreached gap and its decoded body is likely data.

name: clear_record_flag_and_return
description: Stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the pointer register and returns the stacked value. It sits in an unreached gap and its decoded body is likely data.

name: stub_clear_record_flag_one
description: One-instruction routine in an unreached gap that stores a zero byte at a fixed offset from the pointer register and returns the stacked value. The single instruction is too short to confirm a real routine.

name: clear_interrupt_flags_when_set
description: Checks bit five of a global word. When it is set, writes 255 to a global byte, keeps only bit six of a second global, stores the result in a third global, and calls a subroutine.

name: build_sample_period_tables
description: Fills eight records with a data pointer, a half length and a period, the period being a fixed constant of 3579545 divided by a table value. It then adds the code base to two stored offsets to form pointers, fills four entries of a second table, and sets a byte global to 255.

name: build_sample_period_tables
description: Fills eight records with a data pointer, a half length and a period, the period being a fixed constant of 3579545 divided by a table value. It then adds the code base to two stored offsets to form pointers, fills four entries of a second table, and sets a byte global to 255. The listing is identical to the neighbouring table builder.

name: reset_sound_channel_state
description: Clears a byte global, then writes fifteen and 255 into a global control word. The facts show audio and DMA control registers are touched through the routines it calls.

name: advance_sound_channel_sequences
description: Per-tick update for four sound channels. When the playback flag is set, each channel reads command bytes from its stream: a code selects an instrument, sets an effect flag, jumps to a loop pointer or ends the sequence, and otherwise the channel period, volume and sample pointers are written to the audio registers.

name: advance_sound_channels_register_variant
description: Register-based variant of the per-tick channel sequencer for four channels. It reads the same command bytes, writes the audio channel registers, and returns once the channel counter goes below zero.

name: restart_sound_channel_sequence
description: Resets one channel's sequence state, reads command bytes from its stream, and then continues into the shared per-tick update loop until all channels are done.

name: start_sound_channel_instrument
description: Enters the channel sequencer at an instrument selection: it sets the channel's instrument structure from the next stream byte, then processes that channel's command stream until the channel counter runs out.

name: enter_sequencer_at_note_start
description: Entry into the channel sequencer that sets a channel's stream pointer and first note period from a stream byte and a volume multiplier. It then continues into the shared per-tick loop.

name: enter_sequencer_at_command_read
description: Entry into the shared sequencer loop at the point that reads the next command byte from a channel stream. It is reached from one other routine and has no separate work of its own.

name: enter_sequencer_at_flag_set
description: Entry into the sequencer that stores a control flag taken from the next stream byte and then continues into the command loop.

name: enter_sequencer_at_loop_table
description: Entry into the sequencer that loads the next command address from the channel's loop table and reads a command from the stream.

name: start_channel_dma_and_note
description: Writes a DMA control value that sets the channel's enable bit together with the DMA master enable, then processes a note from the stream and enters the shared per-tick loop.

name: update_channel_volume_and_effect
description: Per-tick update for one channel that applies a volume slide from the stored step, scales the volume from the sample data and advances an effect pointer. It then handles the channel's loop bookkeeping.

name: clear_channel_buffer_entry
description: Entry into the sequencer loop that writes a zero byte into a channel buffer at the index in a data register, records that index in the channel state and continues into the per-tick loop.

name: clear_channel_buffer_range
description: Clears a flag bit in the channel state and writes zero bytes into the channel buffer over a range of indices. When the index passes the limit it continues into the per-tick loop.

name: write_sixty_into_channel_buffer
description: Entry into the sequencer loop that writes the value sixty into the channel buffer at the index in a data register, records that index in the channel state and continues into the per-tick loop.

name: combine_word_planes_with_table
description: Combines a block of word planes with values from a global table selected by an argument, using AND, NOT and OR so that each word takes bits from either the source or the destination. It runs over 64 rows of four words each and returns a combined register pair.

name: mask_word_planes_with_table
description: Loops over 160 source words, combining each with a global table value and updating the same word in four spaced destination planes using AND, NOT and OR.

name: store_stack_word_and_call
description: Stores a word taken from the caller's stack into a global, calls one subroutine, and returns the two data registers combined into one 64-bit value.

name: call_helper_then_return
description: Calls one subroutine with no arguments and returns, with no other operations.

name: read_mouse_position_and_clamp
description: Reads the mouse-port movement from the previous sample, applies it to a horizontal position with wraparound, clamps that position to a 640-pixel screen width and halves it. It applies the same wraparound and halving to a vertical position and checks the button bits.

name: store_mouse_movement_deltas
description: Reads the mouse-port movement register and stores its low byte and high byte in two globals as the horizontal and vertical deltas, then calls one subroutine.

name: save_state_and_enable_interrupts
description: Copies one global value into two other globals, then writes a fixed interrupt-enable value with the set bit to the interrupt-enable register.

name: clear_pending_flag_and_restore
description: When a pending flag is set, writes fixed values to the interrupt request and interrupt enable registers, clears the flag and returns the stored word. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: build_copper_list_entries
description: Builds a copper list in memory by writing display control and data-fetch words, choosing one of two display window settings from a global flag. It then fills 32 colour register writes from the parameter table, starting at the first colour register and rising by two.

name: wait_for_interrupt_bit_five
description: Stores its argument in a global and writes the value four higher to the copper pointer register, then spins until bit five of the interrupt request read register is set. It returns the stored value with that bit masked.

name: request_interrupt_and_wait
description: Writes the value 32 to the interrupt request register and spins until bit five of the interrupt request read register is set. It returns that bit.

name: patch_colour_entries_after_marker
description: Searches a list of register-value pairs for the first colour register address and then writes a count of values from the source array into the value slots that follow it, two words apart.

name: unknown_routine_timed_out
description: Decompilation timed out, so only the call list is known. The routine has 21 instructions, is called from one routine, and nothing more can be stated from the evidence.

name: write_sprite_control_header
description: Writes a sprite header into a sprite buffer selected by an index: a start line, a horizontal start, a stop line and control flags. The start line is offset by a fixed amount that changes with a global flag.

name: decode_keyboard_key_code
description: Clears two globals and, when a flag is clear and the low bit of a value is set, reads a key code from the keyboard serial register. Codes below 96 are mapped through a key table whose unshifted row holds the digits, dash, equals and backquote, and the flag is cleared when the low bit is clear.

name: copy_eight_thousand_longwords
description: Copies 8000 longwords from a source address to a destination address, one after another, with no other work.

name: fade_colour_nibbles_by_step
description: Copies a block of colour words into a 32-word stack buffer, then repeatedly decrements each four-bit channel that is not zero. It waits on the vertical position register between passes and stops once every channel reaches zero.

name: call_helper_then_return_result
description: Calls one subroutine with no arguments, then calls a second subroutine with the two arguments and returns that second result.

name: call_helper_then_optional_callback
description: Calls one subroutine with its argument, then calls a second subroutine only when a global value is nonzero.

name: advance_seed_return_high_bits
description: Calls one subroutine, adds 12345 to its result, stores the sum in a global and returns its high fifteen bits.

name: store_high_word_of_argument
description: Decoded from an unreached gap, and the listing only stores the high word of its argument into a global. The call list names library functions that the decompiled body does not show, so the behaviour beyond the store is uncertain.

name: stub_empty_routine_populous
description: Empty routine that performs no operations and returns immediately.

name: allocate_file_record_and_open
description: Allocates a record sized from a table entry and marks it with a four-character tag. It then uses directory, input and open wrappers of the DOS library to set up a file handle, stores the record in a global and returns.

name: tokenize_command_into_argv
description: Splits a command string into words separated by spaces, tabs or line breaks, with double-quoted words and doubled quotes handled. It stores each word in a buffer, then allocates a null-terminated pointer array and fills it with the word addresses.

name: append_string_bounded
description: Appends a source string to the end of a destination string, copying at most about 32767 characters and terminating the result when that limit is reached.

name: append_string_with_count
description: Appends a source string to a destination string, copying at most the number of characters given by the third argument. It writes a terminator if the limit is reached before the source ends.

name: copy_string_pad_zeros
description: Copies bytes from a source string into a destination buffer up to a count, stopping at a null terminator, then fills the remaining count with zero bytes.

name: multiply_halves_cross_terms
description: Computes the cross terms of two 32-bit values from their 16-bit halves and returns a register pair. The high longword is the summed cross terms and the low longword is the second input.

name: open_window_icon_resources
description: Opens a file named by a structure entry through the DOS open wrapper and the icon library, then retrieves a resource with the identifier 1005 and stores it with its pointer in the record. It refers to the WINDOW text, and closes its handles before returning.

name: call_optional_cleanup_then_helper
description: Calls a cleanup function stored in a global when that pointer is set, then calls one subroutine with no arguments.

name: call_optional_cleanup_then_helper
description: Calls a cleanup function stored in a global when that pointer is set, then calls one subroutine with no arguments. The listing is the same as the neighbouring routine.

name: release_loaded_resources
description: Releases resources held in globals: it unlocks file locks in a table, calls a cleanup function when one is set, and frees or closes stored handles. It also writes a stored value through a pointer and calls further library vectors for the remaining handles.

name: close_indexed_file_entry
description: Closes the file handle in the table entry selected by the argument, unless a flag marks that handle as shared, then clears the entry and returns zero. An out-of-range index or empty entry sets an error code of two and returns minus one.
